name: transient-diffusion
title: Transient diffusion: time-stepping
question:
Does a time-stepped `DiffusionProcess` (backward-Euler, dolfinx-backed)
conserve mass under a no-flux boundary while smoothing/decaying an initial
field, when driven through process-bigraph's own Composite tick loop
(not called directly)?
hypothesis:
With no Dirichlet boundary condition (natural Neumann / zero-flux), the
FEM integral of the field should stay flat tick over tick while the
gaussian bump's peak monotonically decays as it spreads.
objective:
Run the `transient_diffusion` composite for several ticks and verify (a)
the field's peak decays as diffusion spreads the initial gaussian bump and
(b) the FEM-integral mass stays conserved (no-flux boundary), exercising
the additive-delta store convention through a real Composite.run(), not
just DiffusionProcess.update() in isolation.
description:
Wires a single `DiffusionProcess` (Task 3) to shared `stores.solution`/
`stores.source` and a `RAMEmitter`, seeded with a nodal gaussian bump. The
process returns a DELTA each tick (new field - previous field) so the
shared `array[float]` store composes additively -- the same convention
`reaction-diffusion` (this investigation's headline study) relies on to
couple a second process into `stores.source`.

expected_behavior.name: mass-conserved
expected_behavior.en: The FEM integral of the field drifts by less than 5% between the first and last recorded tick.
expected_behavior.condition: relative drift in field_integral over the run < 5%
expected_behavior.rationale: No Dirichlet BC is applied (natural Neumann/zero-flux boundary), so mass can redistribute within the domain but not leave it; the FEM integral of the field should stay flat tick over tick up to solver noise.

expected_behavior.name: peak-decays
expected_behavior.en: The field's maximum at the final recorded tick is strictly less than at the first recorded tick.
expected_behavior.rationale: Diffusion spreads a concentrated gaussian bump over time; the field's maximum should monotonically decrease as mass redistributes toward a flatter profile.

behavior_tests.name: mass-conserved
behavior_tests.description:
The FEM integral of the field (a mass-bookkeeping sensor reading,
recomputed fresh every tick) must not drift by more than 5% between the
first and last recorded tick.

provenance.note: Zero-flux (natural Neumann) boundary conditions conserve the domain integral exactly in the continuous problem; 5% is a numerical-noise margin for the discrete backward-Euler solve.

behavior_tests.name: peak-decays
behavior_tests.description:
max(solution) at the final recorded tick must be strictly less than
max(solution) at the first recorded tick.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition:
Mass conservation and peak decay both pass, confirming the time-stepped
DiffusionProcess wrapper is trustworthy before reaction-diffusion
couples a second process into its shared stores.

embed_visualizations.name: field-animation
embed_visualizations.description: Interactive Plotly animation of the diffusing field over time (peak decay + mass conservation).
